caseno: Appeal from Appellate Decree No.307 of 1963.
lawyer:
M. A. Aziz ------ For the appellant. 
Habibur Rahman Khan ------ For respondents No. 1(1), 1(3), 1(5), 1(7) & 2.
parties:
Gaher Ali Mandal  ------ Appellant.
Vs.
Manik Sikder and others ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
The facts leading to this appeal in brief are that the suit land originally belonged to on Umesh Chandra Ghose but it was wrongly recorded in the name of one Mahim Chandra Ghose and others at the time of C. S. operation. The heirs of Mahim Chandra and others however executed a deed of relinquishment in favour of Umesh. Umesh Chandra executed a kabuliyat in favour of the land lords. Thereafter, Umesh settled 7'00 acres out of 12'36 acres with one Mulfat Mondal who sold the same to one Jatindra Nath in 1352 B. S. who again settled the said 7'00 acres with the plaintiff in 1354 B. S. The plaintiff also obtained settlement if the remaining 5,36 acres of land from Umesh Chandra in 1358 B. S. Thus the plaintiff became the owner of the entire 12'36, acres of land out of which he sold 2'00 acres to one Rabia and was in possession of the balance of 10'36 acres which is the disputed land in the present suit. It was further asserted by the plaintiff that he had transplanted boro paddy in the suit land and the same was forcibly cut away by the defendants in Baisakh, 1365 B. S. The plaintiff has thereby suffered a loss of 150 maunds of paddy and he claimed compensation for the said quantity of paddy at the rate of Tk. 15/- per maund. 

 Those are the barga kabuliyats (exhibit 1 series), rent receipts (exhibit 5 series) and the judgment and decree obtained by the plaintiff's predecessors in a Money suit in respect of a part of the suit land (exhibits 9 and 10). The finding of the learned Subordinate Judge on the question of possession does not also appear to be conclusive. He has merely expressed his doubts if the plaintiff could retain his possession after the judgments of the criminal cases. Be that as it may, the title having been found in favour of the plaintiff by both the courts below, the status of the defendants is nothing more than that of a trespasser. Therefore, even if the plaintiff is out of possession as found by the learned Subordinate Judge, the plaintiff as the rightful owner is entitled to maintain this suit for compensation for the paddy grown on his land. In support of his contention Mr. Aziz has cited the case of Murulidhar Agarwala and others Vs. Rupendra Nath Mitter and another reported in 56 C.W.N. at page 260. In the said case the plaintiff sued the defendants for damages for use and occupation or in the alternative for mesne prat on the allegation that the defendants were in wrongful occupation as trespasser and the plaintiff's title was sufficiency proved but he was found to be out of possession; it was held that the suit was maintainable in law. I am in agreement with the decision referred to above. In the instant case also the plaintiff's title has been found by both the courts below. While the trial court found possession in favour of the plaintiff, the lower appellate court found it in favour of the defendants. The reaping away of the paddy is admitted but the trial court found that the plaintiff had grown the paddy whereas the court of appeal below held that it was grown by the defendants. Since the plaintiff has been found to be the rightful owner, he is entitled to the paddy grown on his land. If the defendants had chosen to grow paddy on some body else's land, they have done so at their own risk and peril and must pay for it. I am therefore, clearly of the opinion that the suit for compensation irrespective of the plaintiff's possession was maintainable at his instance when he has been able to prove his title in the suit land.
